questions.stem: By what other name is Data Syndication known?
questions.explanation: Syndication is also known as synchronisation.

questions.stem: Which statement about Data Syndication is correct?
options: It is a technology that must be bought from a vendor
It is a database feature available only in the cloud
It is a process, not a technology
It is another name for a data warehouse
It can only handle structured input
questions.explanation: Data Syndication is a process, not a technology, so any expensive or cheap technology can be used to implement it.

options: Encrypting data before it leaves the organisation
Removing duplicate records from master data
Collecting and preparing an up-to-date dataset for a particular activity
questions.explanation: Data Syndication is to collect and prepare an up-to-date dataset for a particular activity, such as a marketing campaign.

questions.stem: Which example illustrates Data Syndication in *I Am Datapedia!*?
options: Preparing a dataset from multiple source systems for the marketing team to plan an upcoming campaign
Running a DISTINCT command on an age column
Copying a source data model into a landing zone
Retraining a model after product types increase
Generating fake customer records for developers
questions.explanation: The example given is preparing a dataset from multiple source systems so the marketing team can plan its campaign exercise.

questions.stem: What is the meaning of the Greek word 'syndikos', from which 'syndicate' ultimately derives?
questions.explanation: The Greek 'syndikos' means caretaker of an issue, comparable to an ombudsman or representative; the French 'syndicat' means trade union.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT listed as a capability of a Data Syndication process?
options: Handling any type of format as input and output
Providing monitoring dashboards and reports for compliance and audit trails
Automatically generating a physical data model
questions.explanation: Format flexibility, alerts, access matrix and compliance monitoring are all listed; generating a physical data model is not.

questions.stem: In what forms can a Data Syndication process deliver its output?
options: Email, SMS, spreadsheet, database, ML models and other formats designed to customer requirements
questions.explanation: Output formats can be designed to customer requirements and sent as email, SMS, spreadsheet, database, ML models and more.

questions.stem: How do third-party data syndication companies make money?
options: By collecting and preparing syndicated datasets and selling them as a DaaS service
By charging per query run in the cloud
By building data warehouses for clients
questions.explanation: Specialist syndication companies collect and prepare relevant syndicated datasets for large organisations and sell them as Data as a Service.

questions.stem: Why has a Data Syndication process become so important in the current era?
options: Because databases no longer support joins
Because so many sources and channels produce structured, semi-structured and unstructured data, such as social media, CCTV, audio, emails, PDFs and scans
Because marketing teams no longer use data
questions.explanation: With data arriving from many channels and in many formats, organisations need a process to syndicate it into a usable dataset.

questions.stem: Which use of syndicated customer behavioural data does *I Am Datapedia!* suggest?
options: Deciding which database vendor to buy
questions.explanation: Collecting customer behavioural data from all the various channels can help many organisations plan their production.
